comments.text: [NC first-hand] LoadAnm(this, anmIdx, path, spriteIdxOffset). Signature matches the TH06 community reconstruction parameter for parameter.
[NC first-hand] Resolves a script-relative sprite index against the manager's per-anm sprite base table and stores it into vm+0x100.
[NC first-hand] Main draw path. Reads the anchor field (vm+0xc4 & 0x700) and compares it by value, not by bit -- see the anchor enum.
[NC first-hand] Scans the script for an opcode-22 label matching vm+0x8a, remembering the -1 (default) label. Opcode 22 is a no-op during execution.
[NC first-hand] ANM v0 script interpreter. Instruction header is {s16 time; u8 opcode; u8 args_size} with args at +4; dispatch is a 36-entry jump table at 0x140007494 bounded by CMP DL,0x23.
CMP DL,0x23 / JA: opcodes above 35 fall through to the advance tail. No shipped .anm uses an opcode >= 36.
Shared handler for PosTimeLinear/Decel/Accel; they differ only in flag bits.
AND [vm+0xc4],0xfffffcff / OR [vm+0xc4],0x400 -> anchor field 4 = (left, top). Zero-argument, absolute assignment.
AND [vm+0xc4],0xfffffbff / OR [vm+0xc4],0x300 -> anchor field 3 = (center, top). Zero-argument, absolute assignment.
AND [vm+0xc4],0xfffff9ff / OR [vm+0xc4],0x100 -> anchor field 1 = (left, center). Zero-argument, absolute assignment.
AND [vm+0xc4],0xfffffaff / OR [vm+0xc4],0x200 -> anchor field 2 = (right, center). Zero-argument, absolute assignment.
AND [vm+0xc4],0xfffffdff / OR [vm+0xc4],0x500 -> anchor field 5 = (right, top). Zero-argument, absolute assignment.
next = current + 4 + args_size. Also the direct jump-table target for the execution-time no-ops (opcode 6 nop, opcode 22 interruptLabel).

[NC first-hand] Rebuilds the layout-aware scancode remap table at 0x140c21e60 via GetKeyboardLayout/MapVirtualKeyExW, then feeds the logical button bitmap builder. This is why the cheat is typed as letters, not key positions.

Shared bullet-pattern handler for opcodes 67..75 and 201 (jump-table slot 60). Stores aim_mode = opcode - 67 into bullet_props+0x30, so opcode 201 selects 134 -- a mode the consumer at 0x14000f870 does not implement (its switch covers 0..8 with no default), leaving the angle at its pre-switch 0.0. Settled, not provisional.

NC opcode 200, the one genuinely new ECL instruction: a polar form of TH06's SHOOTOFFSET (opcode 81). Writes enemy+0xc5c = (cos(arg0)*arg1, sin(arg0)*arg1, 0); the z zero comes from R12D, cleared by XOR R12D,R12D at 0x14002213f. arg2 unused.
Shared handler for 2 opcodes: 85 LASERCREATE, 86 LASERCREATEAIMED.

[TH06 baseline + NC verified] Stage timeline interpreter. Runtime dispatch remains limited to opcodes 0..12 and advances by the int16 size field at +0x06.

[NC first-hand] Per-enemy tick. Identified because CC0 TH06 has exactly two callers of CalcKillBoxCollision (BulletManager::OnUpdate and EnemyManager::OnUpdate) and NC has exactly two as well, one already independently named BulletManager__OnUpdate. Content confirms it: hitbox scaled by 1/1.5, life -= 10 on a body hit, damage clamped to 70, then the spellcard divisors.
Loader scan for an opcode-13 timeline checkpoint.

[NC first-hand] Player init: loads the player ANM, sets the spawn position (192, 384, 0.49), the hitbox RADIUS 1.25 at +0x774c and grabItemSize (12, 12, 5) at +0x9f28. All of those match TH06 numerically.

[NC first-hand] Player per-frame tick, registered as a chain callback (hence no direct xrefs). Tests the logical button bitmap at 0x140a6ec60: bomb on a press edge of bit 1, focus flag stored to player+0x785c from bit 2, an 8-case movement switch on the direction bits, shooting on bit 0. TH06 splits this into OnUpdate + HandlePlayerInputs (2282 + 3482 bytes); NC inlined them (5309).

=== Player__UpdatePlayerBullets (inlined here; a standalone function in CC0 TH06) ===
Starts by decrementing laserTimer[0] and [1] (CC0's 2-iteration loop, unrolled), then walks bullets[80]: branch on bulletType, advance position, recycle when out of bounds or the anm script ends.
range 0x140069740-0x140069b03

=== Player__SpawnBullets (inlined here; a standalone function in CC0 TH06) ===
Scans bullets[80] for a free slot (bulletState == 0), picks the plain or focus callback by isFocused and calls it; see FIRE_BULLET_RESULT for the return codes.
range 0x140069bd1-0x140069c6a

[NC first-hand] Player bullets vs one enemy. Walks bullets[80] doing an AABB overlap test against (enemyPos, enemyHitboxSize) and accumulates bullet->damage (only a third of it while a bomb is active), then walks the 32 bomb regions and adds their damage. Sets *hitWithLazerDuringBomb when a bomb region connects while bombInfo.isInUse. Called from EnemyManager__OnUpdate right after the body check.

[NC first-hand, our own name] The one data-driven fire-bullet implementation. TH06 has four hand-written FireBullet{ReimuA,ReimuB,MarisaA,MarisaB}; NC replaced them with 26-byte thunks that each pass a CharacterPowerData table to this. No upstream name to borrow, because upstream has no such function.
[NC first-hand] 26-byte thunk: passes the ReimuA CharacterPowerData table to Player__FireBulletFromTable. Selected via g_CharData[0].
[NC first-hand] 26-byte thunk: passes the ReimuB CharacterPowerData table to Player__FireBulletFromTable. Selected via g_CharData[1].
[NC first-hand] 26-byte thunk: passes the MarisaA CharacterPowerData table to Player__FireBulletFromTable. Selected via g_CharData[2].
[NC first-hand] 26-byte thunk: passes the MarisaB CharacterPowerData table to Player__FireBulletFromTable. Selected via g_CharData[3].

[NC first-hand, our own name] Walks the bomb-projectile array at player+0x7754, skips entries whose x extent is 0, and AABB-tests each against the caller's box using half extents. CC0 has this logic INLINED inside Player::CheckGraze, so there is no upstream name to borrow -- note this is the opposite of NC's usual direction, which inlines more than TH06 rather than less.

[NC first-hand] Death collision against a bullet box. Runs the bomb-projectile clip test first (0x14006a8c0), and on a hit spawns the death particles, sets the death state and enqueues sound 4 (SOUND_PICHUN) -- TH06's Player::Die is inlined here. NOT graze: the only function that enqueues sound 30 (SOUND_GRAZE) for bullets is BulletManager__OnUpdate, so CheckGraze/ScoreGraze are inlined there. The extra char parameter selects circle-vs-AABB (0) or circle-vs-circle (1).

[NC first-hand] Laser collision. The signature matches CC0's CalcLaserHitbox(laserCenter, laserSize, rotation, angle, canGraze) parameter for parameter, and it calls cosf/sinf for the rotation plus the graze particle effect.
[NC first-hand] Runs the keyboard cheat, then an inlined 4-step XInput pad cheat over the 0x140c21e58 bitmap (hold L3+R3, Y, X, hold LB+RB). Either success sets the score.dat dirty flag at +0x9e99.

[NC first-hand] Types-the-password cheat. Edge-detects the 8 letters of the 0x14030c520 table, walks "classiclager" via +0x4430, and on the 12th letter fills the CLRD table with 99. Wrong letter resets to 0, 'c' restarts at 1.
Writes 10 bytes of 99 at 0x1404ff100 + n*0x18 for n in 0..3.
Enqueues sound id 0x1c (SOUND_1UP in the TH06 numbering) into g_SoundRequestQueue.
[NC first-hand] Result-screen per-frame tick. Switches on +0x9e94 through the 18-entry jump table at 0x140072824; only state 6 (Lunatic records) reaches the cheat call at 0x14006fab4.
Jump-table target for state 6 (Lunatic records). Only this state calls the unlock cheats; states 3/4/5/7 enter the shared handler directly.
Shared records-page handler for result-screen states 3..7.
[NC first-hand] Serializes HSCR/CLRD/CATK/PSCR and writes score.dat. The whole body is gated on the +0x9e99 dirty flag, which the unlock cheats set.
8 x {int ch; int dik;} decode table for the classiclager cheat.
[NC first-hand] Score. A graze adds 500, same as TH06.
[NC first-hand] Per-stage graze counter, capped at 99999. TH06 caps it at 9999 (CC0 Player::ScoreGraze) -- this is the one graze number NC actually changed.
[NC first-hand] Total graze counter, capped at 999999 (same as TH06).
Four 0x18-byte CLRD records; clear flags start at +0x0c.
CLRD[0] clear flags: 5 with-retries + 5 without-retries bytes.
[NC first-hand] Non-zero suppresses graze counting, same as TH06.
Three int slots; negative means free. Cheat enqueues 28 (SOUND_1UP).
Non-zero skips sound enqueueing; exact meaning still unconfirmed.
